Jonas / team,

Preliminary triage notes (SRE):
- Root cause: rollout bug in the backpressure/rate-cap policy engine. A recent change to the default tenant policy selector caused a small percentage of tenants to inherit a low-capacity policy intended for preview clusters.
- Symptom: these tenants got stricter per-tenant queue thresholds leading to premature 429s under short bursts. The reject reason in logs is "quota_policy_mismatch" and the x-redwood-rate-limit headers show lowered values.
- Scope: Roughly 8 of our larger tenants saw transient 429 spikes; FinixPay accounts for ~40% of that traffic window per our telemetry.

Mitigation performed:
1) Immediate rollback of the policy selector change to restore correct default policy (completed 16:05 PT).
2) Enabled per-tenant bypass for FinixPay to route through a more permissive backpressure path (temporary, completed 16:12 PT).
3) Staging a hotfix that validates policy source (preview vs prod) before applying — will roll to prod 2026-08-04 02:00 UTC (ETA ~11 hours).

Next steps for customer remediation:
- We'll provide a list of affected request ids and estimated failed transactions (CSV attached in follow-up).
- Propose a one-time credit equivalent to two days of token/ingress spend for impacted capacity (pending leadership approval).
- Postmortem to be shared within 48 hours and a follow-up call to review changes.

I'll paste the short log snippet below for your ops team: 

"2026-08-03T15:52:18Z x-redwood-reject: quota_policy_mismatch tenant=finixpay shard=us-west-2\nRequest-ID: rwd-8b7a-21f4"

Evelyn

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for the timeline and endpoint list. Confirming the plan and deliverables: 

1) Immediate (completed)
- Rolled back the policy selector (completed 2026-08-03 16:05 PT).
- Enabled temporary per-tenant bypass for FinixPay (completed 2026-08-03 16:12 PT).

2) Short-term (within 24 hours)
- Hotfix deployment to validate policy source before applying (scheduled 2026-08-04 02:00 UTC).
- Detailed CSV of affected request ids and estimated failed transactions (we will upload to the Drive link below by 18:00 PT).

3) Mid-term (2 weeks)
- Add automated canary checks for policy selector changes, including synthetic traffic tests.
- Add an alert rule to detect "quota_policy_mismatch" reject reasons and auto-escalate to on-call.

4) Customer remediation
- Proposed credit: one-time operational credit equal to two days of average ingress/compute for impacted endpoints. Exact number: $8,400 — will be applied as a credit on your next monthly invoice and visible as "Service Credit - Incident INC-2243". (Pending finance approval; initiating now.)

5) Postmortem & follow-up
- Post-incident write-up uploaded to Drive by 2026-08-05 16:00 PT: https://drive.redwood.com/incident/finixpay-20260804
- 30-minute review call scheduled for today 10:30 PT (confirmed).

If FinixPay would like us to extend the temporary bypass longer while you complete customer-facing verification, we can do that — let us know the window you need.

Apologies for the disruption and thanks for working with us so quickly. We'll follow up after the hotfix rollout with validation metrics demonstrating the fix.
